Morphological analysis starts from a given word and produces its morphosyntactic description or sequence of morphological tags [E1]. Morphological inflection, by contrast, starts from a lemma together with a set of morphological tags and produces the corresponding inflected word form [E2]. So, analysis is essentially word-form-to-tags, while inflection is lemma-plus-tags-to-word-form [E1][E2].

supported_claims.claim: Applying cyclical learning rate (CLR) has positive impacts on NMT training for both Adam and SGD.

For SGD, CLR removes the need for a large initial learning rate by helping the optimizer explore local minima better, and using shrinking with CLR for SGD is not desirable because a higher learning rate is required.
For Adam, applying CLR produces consistent improvements regardless of shrink options, and the gains from CLR are more significant for Adam than for SGD.
The paper contrasts the CLR decay policy with the standard inverse square root (INV) policy, where INV uses warm-up to a maximum learning rate followed by reciprocal square-root decay.
